title: Decode: DSA exact top-k + DCP merge
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows), L≈135K (local ≈33.75K on DCP4), k=3; also r1 (16 rows), r8 (128 rows)
basis: baseline MEASURED in-step (gap512 EP16 B92 profile); achievable = rhea1n model_rows B96_L135K: DSA.topk 46.1 us + P8 DCP top-k merge 180.7 us per step (24 DSA layers: 1.9 + 7.5 us/layer); r8 (B32): 15.4 + ~154 us
gap_analysis: Seeded from gap512: topk_merge_kernel<16> 52-77 us/layer vs 6-7 modelled; topk_pp_hist/window/win 25-45 us vs 1.4. Code read (dcp_exchange decode wiring): launch_params bounds the local length by max_model_len/DCP (1M/4 = 262144 keys), which forces cluster=2 CTAs per row (WRITE bitmap holds 131072 keys/CTA) and segmax=0 (keys streamed from global) at every batch, and the pre-pass on, independent of the real contexts (~34K local). PDL is hard-off on the merge (s_pdl_rows = 0) because the trtllm-gen sparse core reads counts before griddepcontrol.wait. Phase breakdown pending (bench with per-row dbg stamps).
inefficiencies: launch shape bounded by max_model_len (1M), not the step's contexts: 2 CTAs/row + streamed keys + pre-pass everywhere (code read; cost to be measured)
pre-pass = 3 kernels (hist, window, win) + merge kernel WRITE pass: logits read >= 3x (code read)
merge kernel PDL off (consumer reads counts before its wait); serial launch chain on the critical stream
1 NVLink round + tie round per row with flag polls in 2 CTAs/row (hypothesis: latency-bound, to be measured with dbg stamps)
rubin_features: NVLink multicast (multimem.st) for the candidate/histogram exchange
thread-block clusters + DSMEM for per-row parallel histogram reduce
PDL (griddepcontrol) chaining with the indexer logits kernel and the sparse core
TMA bulk loads of logits tiles
plan: 1. 4-GPU microbench (DCP4 group) of the in-tree DcpExchange top-k at r1/r8/r24, L=135K, realistic logits; per-kernel CUPTI times + per-row phase stamps + path stats
2. root-cause the merge/pre-pass time (ncu on the merge kernel)
3. redesign: single-pass histogram select over the whole GPU, one multicast exchange, parallel resolve + WRITE, PDL
4. exactness unit test vs stock (bitwise selection sets), graph-safe tie/overflow path
5. microbench vs model at r1/r8/r24; step A/B with INFRA harness; landed-ready
